<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914440_theRebbe_936" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914440_theRebbe_936__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the Torah is called an inheritance due to the refinement of sparks from Tohu, but one must prepare oneself to study Torah that is not an inheritance, which refers to the essence of Torah drawn through study for its own sake.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And this is that the Torah is called an inheritance, and nevertheless they said, "Prepare yourself to study Torah, which is not an inheritance,"</t>
    <t s="1">for that the Torah is called an inheritance is from the aspect of the clarifications [that come] through the Torah.</t>
    <t s="2">For the sparks that are in physical things,</t>
    <t s="3">and likewise the sparks that are in the intellect of the animal soul,</t>
    <t s="4">their source is in Tohu,</t>
    <t s="5">and the source of the souls of Israel is in Tikkun.</t>
    <t s="6">For this is that Esav is called "great" and Yaakov is called "small,"</t>
    <t s="7">because the root of Esav is in Tohu,</t>
    <t s="8">for the lights of Tohu are abundant lights</t>
    <t s="9">(great),</t>
    <t s="10">and the root of Yaakov is in Tikkun,</t>
    <t s="11">for the lights of Tikkun are limited lights and are bounded within vessels</t>
    <t s="12">(small).</t>
    <t s="13">And since Yaakov and Esav are brothers,</t>
    <t s="14">as it is written,</t>
    <t s="15">"Is not Esav a brother to Yaakov,"</t>
    <t s="16">and brothers inherit from one another,</t>
    <t s="17">therefore,</t>
    <t s="18">by means of the souls of Israel clarifying the sparks,</t>
    <t s="19">they inherit the lights of Tohu.</t>
    <t s="20">And what is said, "Prepare yourself to study Torah, which is not an inheritance for you," is regarding the Torah as it is above the matter of clarifications,</t>
    <t s="21">for the drawing down of this aspect of Torah is through the study of Torah for its own sake.</t>
    <t s="22">And this is "prepare yourself to study Torah,"</t>
    <t s="23">that one must toil himself so that his study be for its own sake, without any ulterior motive at all</t>
    <t s="24">(even not the motive to refine his soul),</t>
    <t s="25">and through the study of Torah for its own sake, he draws down the Torah as it is in its own essence.</t>
    <t s="26">For this level of Torah is above even the lights of Tohu</t>
    <t s="27">(which Israel inherit through the work of clarifications),</t>
    <t s="28">which is not an inheritance for you.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section compares Torah to rain and dew, where rain comes through refinement from below and dew is a revelation from above, corresponding to Torah studied for self-refinement and Torah studied for its own sake.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And this is, "May my teaching drop as the rain, my speech flow as the dew,"</t>
    <t s="2">for rain comes from clouds that are made from the moisture of the earth,</t>
    <t s="3">"and a mist ascended from the earth and watered the entire face of the ground."</t>
    <t s="4">And dew comes from above.</t>
    <t s="5">For so it is in spirituality,</t>
    <t s="6">that rain is the matter</t>
    <t s="7">that comes through clarification, refinement, and elevation of that which is below,</t>
    <t s="8">as the statement of our sages, of blessed memory,</t>
    <t s="9">on the verse "May my teaching drop as the rain,"</t>
    <t s="10">that when creatures break their stubbornness, immediately rain descends,</t>
    <t s="11">and dew is a revelation from above.</t>
    <t s="12">And the reason that the Torah is compared to dew and to rain is,</t>
    <t s="13">because in the Torah there are these two matters.</t>
    <t s="14">The matter of the descent of the Torah below in order to clarify the world,</t>
    <t s="15">the drawing down of this aspect of Torah is through the study of Torah for one's own sake—"May my teaching drop as the rain,"</t>
    <t s="16">and the Torah as it is in its own essence</t>
    <t s="17">(as it is in Atzilus,</t>
    <t s="18">above its descent into BiY"A),</t>
    <t s="19">the drawing down of this aspect of Torah is through engaging in Torah for its own sake—"my speech flow as the dew."</t>
    <t s="20">And perhaps it can be said that regarding this they said,</t>
    <t s="21">"Whoever reads and reviews, the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews opposite him,"</t>
    <t s="22">that through engaging in Torah for its own sake, there is the drawing down and revelation of the Torah as it is from the aspect above,</t>
    <t s="23">the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews,</t>
    <t s="24">the dew of Torah.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the rain of Torah corresponds to the revealed aspect of Torah, where the Divine light is concealed and requires refinement, while the dew of Torah corresponds to the inner dimension of Torah, where the light is revealed.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="1">that these two matters</t>
    <t s="2">(the rain of Torah and the dew of Torah)</t>
    <t s="3">are the revealed aspect of Torah and the inner dimension of Torah.</t>
    <t s="4">For in the revealed aspect of Torah, which is clothed in physical matters,</t>
    <t s="5">the Divine light is in concealment,</t>
    <t s="6">and in order for the light to be revealed in the person who studies the Torah, it is through his refining himself,</t>
    <t s="7">for this is that "if he merits, it becomes for him an elixir of life,"</t>
    <t s="8">for through his meriting—from the term refinement—then specifically it becomes for him an elixir of life.</t>
    <t s="9">And in the inner dimension of Torah, the Divine light is revealed.</t>
    <t s="10">And to add,</t>
    <t s="11">that even after a person refines himself,</t>
    <t s="12">so that then even in the revealed aspect of Torah the light is revealed,</t>
    <t s="13">it is not like the revelation that is in the inner dimension of Torah.</t>
    <t s="14">For since the light in the revealed aspect of Torah is clothed in physical matters that conceal the light,</t>
    <t s="15">therefore even after the removal of the concealment, the light is not as revealed as the light in the inner dimension of Torah.</t>
    <t s="16">And this is that the revealed aspect of Torah is the rain of Torah,</t>
    <t s="17">[with] two matters in this.</t>
    <t s="18">That in the study of the revealed aspect of Torah, there must be the work of "meriting,"</t>
    <t s="19">the study for one's own sake to refine his soul—in the manner of the matter of "when creatures break their stubbornness."</t>
    <t s="20">And even then,</t>
    <t s="21">the Divine light that shines to the person is as it is clothed in the world—rain.</t>
    <t s="22">And the matter of the dew of Torah is in the inner dimension of Torah.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
